d: Two suspicious bags are taken away for a second look after sniffer dogs raise the alarm, plus a look at the precautions that officers take when they have to go off-site for a job.

At Dublin Airport, Bruce Hellar becomes suspicious after an international traveller enters the country with only one small bag, plus customs workers in Cork search for suspicious items on a cargo ship transporting bananas.
Luggage belonging to two young men returning to Dublin from Ibiza tests positive for drugs, while the hunt is on for illegal cigarettes in Ireland's southwest.
A father gets caught speeding with his newborn baby on board, a migraine causes a mess on the back roads, and a rider gives an unusual excuse for speeding on a Harley.
A nose-to-tail could turn into a fistfight, a group of Kiwis are behaving badly on the roads, and a person gets two tickets in one day.
A driver collides with police after a dangerous overtaking move, and a suspected drink driver cannot blow into the breathalyser and is too afraid of needles to give a blood sample.

An early-morning beer leads to trouble for one driver. Officer Grant issues a ticket to the speediest vehicle he's ever encountered on duty. Meanwhile, a makeshift repair involving string holds a car door in place.
It's a difficult start to the new year for motorists who are still feeling the consequences of the New Year's Eve festivities.
A pirate gets stranded on his way home. A vehicle parks dangerously in Nelson and a tailgater has three different licence plates.
A truck falls over a ledge. And a Mustang blocks traffic on a Taranaki highway.
